Q1 BC857 in SOT-23, Q3 IRLML6402 in SOT-23. U2 MAX3485 in SO-8. J3/J8 are 2x15 SMD. J4/J9 are JST EH 3-pin. J1 is JST XH 2-pin. J11 is JST PH 2-pin. J7 is JST PH 4-pin. All seem appropriate.

Now, check the values of capacitors. C4 0.1u, C1/C5/C6/C8 100u. Spec says C1-C4 100u, C5 0.1u. So the 0.1u is C4, not C5. That's fine. But wait: the spec says C5 is 0.1u decoupling on +3V3. Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. Now, check the values of capacitors. C4 0.1u, C1/C5/C6/C8 100u. Spec says C1-C4 100u, C5 0.1u. So the 0.1u is C4, not C5. That's fine. But wait: the spec says C5 is 0.1u decoupling on +3V3. Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's typical. Not an issue.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.

Actual C4 is 0.1u on +3V3. So the decoupling cap is present. The bulk caps are C1, C5, C6, C8. So C5 is 100u, not 0.1u. That's a ref shift. No issue.

Now, check if there is any missing pull-up on the MAX3485 A line. R16 2k is present. B line has R24 2.2k pull-up and R21 2.2k pull-down. DE/RE has R11 20k pull-down. All present.

Now, check the auto-direction transistor base. R7 10k pull-up to +3V3, R4 5.1k to TXD2. That's a voltage divider. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V? Actually, if TXD2 is high, it's 3.3V. R7 is from +3V3 to base, R4 from base to TXD2. Both ends at 3.3V, so base is 3.3V. Vbe=0, Q1 off. When TXD2 is low (0V), base is at 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1) = 1.11V. Vbe = 3.3 - 1.11 = 2.19V, Q1 on. That's correct. The base current is (3.3-1.11)/10k? Actually, current through R7 is (3.3-1.11)/10k = 0.219mA. Current through R4 is (1.11-0)/5.1k = 0.218mA. So base current is about 0.219mA. That's enough to saturate Q1? Q1 collector current is (3.3V)/20k = 0.165mA when off? Actually when Q1 is on, collector is pulled to 3.3V, so no current through R11. When Q1 is off, collector is pulled to 0 by R11, so current through R11 is 3.3/20k = 0.165mA. So Q1 only needs to sink 0.165mA. Base current 0.219mA is plenty. So it works.

Now, check the MAX3485 DE/RE. When Q1 is on, collector is at 3.3V. DE/RE high. When Q1 is off, collector is at 0V via R11. DE/RE low. Correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 DI. It's connected to TXD2 directly. So when TXD2 is high, DI high. When TXD2 low, DI low. The driver is enabled when TXD2 low. So the start bit (low) is driven. That's correct.

Now, check the MAX3485 RO. It's connected to RXD2. When receiver enabled (DE/RE low), RO follows the bus. When driver enabled (DE/RE high), RO is disabled? Actually, when DE high, ~RE high, receiver disabled, RO is high-impedance. But RXD2 is an input to the M5Stack, so it might float. However, the M5Stack UART RX pin might have an internal pull-up. That's typical. Not an issue.

Now, check the power switch. Q3 IRLML6402. Source to battery, drain to M-BUS pin29. Gate to R3 47k to source, and SW2.2. SW2.3 to GND. When switch is open, gate is pulled to source via R3, Vgs=0, off. When switch is closed, gate is pulled to GND, Vgs=-Vbat, on. Correct.

Now, check the battery connector. J11.1 to Q3.S and R3.2. J11.2 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the external 5V. J1.1 to D2.A, J1.2 to GND. D2.K to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the servo power. +5V to D3.A, D3.K to servo rail. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +5V. J3.27 and J8.27 to +5V. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS +3V3. J3.11 and J8.11 to +3V3. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS BAT. J3.29 and J8.29 to Q3.D. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS GND. J3.2,4,6 and J8.2,4,6 to GND. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS TXD2/RXD2. J3.15 and J8.15 to U2.DI and R4/R7. J3.16 and J8.16 to U2.RO. Correct.

Now, check the M-BUS PortB GPIOs. J3.9 and J8.9 to J7.3. J3.3 and J8.3 to J7.4. Correct.

Now, check the PWM jumpers. J3.19 and J8.19 to R2.2. R2.1 to /NET0006. R13.1 to /NET0006, R13.2 to J3.21/J8.21. R15.2 to /NET0006, R15.1 to J4.3. So ch1 signal can be connected to pin19 or pin21 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J4.3. Correct.

Ch2: J3.20/J8.20 to R23.2. R23.1 to /NET0039. R18.1 to /NET0039, R18.2 to J3.22/J8.22. R17.2 to /NET0039, R17.1 to J9.3. So ch2 signal can be connected to pin20 or pin22 via 0Ω jumpers, and then through 1k to J9.3. Correct.

Serial: R22 bridges J4.3 and J9.3. R1 connects U2.A to J9.3. So both servo pins tied to U2.A. Correct.

Now, is there any issue with the 1k resistors in serial mode? In serial mode, R15 and R17 are still connected between the servo pins and /NET0006 and /NET0039. If the 0Ω jumpers R13/R2/R18/R23 are left open, then /NET0006 and /NET0039 are floating. So the 1k resistors are just hanging. That's fine. But what if someone populates both PWM and serial jumpers? That would connect the PWM GPIOs to the serial bus, causing contention. But the spec says mutually exclusive. So not an anomaly.
